tax.sections.wk.name: Work expenses
tax.sections.wk.guidance.belongs: Work equipment, professional literature, training and further education, union and professional association fees, application costs, business trips, a home office.
tax.sections.wk.guidance.excludes: Commuting to your regular workplace, which is claimed through the distance allowance per kilometre, not with fuel receipts. Clothing you can also wear privately.
tax.sections.wk.guidance.note: Work expenses only pay off above the employee lump sum (Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag); the tax office applies whichever is higher.
tax.sections.va.name: Insurance and pension contributions
tax.sections.va.guidance.belongs: Health and long-term care insurance, liability, accident and occupational disability insurance, pension contributions including Riester and Rürup.
tax.sections.va.guidance.excludes: Property insurance such as household contents, building or comprehensive car cover.
tax.sections.va.guidance.note: Many insurers and pension providers report contributions to the tax office electronically, so compare with their statements.
tax.sections.sa.name: Special expenses
tax.sections.sa.guidance.belongs: Church tax paid directly, donations and membership fees to charitable organisations and political parties, your own first vocational training or first degree.
tax.sections.sa.guidance.excludes: Church tax withheld from your salary; it comes from the wage tax certificate.
tax.sections.sa.guidance.receipts: Donation receipts (Zuwendungsbestätigung); for small donations the bank statement is often enough.
tax.sections.sa.guidance.note: Donations need a recipient that is recognised as charitable.
tax.sections.ab.name: Extraordinary burdens
tax.sections.ab.guidance.belongs: Illness costs you paid yourself (doctor, dentist, medication, glasses, therapy), care costs, disability-related costs.
tax.sections.ab.guidance.excludes: Anything reimbursed by insurance, preventive or wellness offers.
tax.sections.ab.guidance.receipts: Invoices, prescriptions, and for some treatments a medical certificate issued beforehand.
tax.sections.ab.guidance.note: Only the part above your reasonable own share (zumutbare Belastung) counts; the tax office calculates it from your income and family situation.
tax.sections.hh.name: Household services and craftsmen (§35a EStG)
tax.sections.hh.guidance.belongs: Household services (cleaning, gardening, caretaker, chimney sweep, winter service) and craftsmen's work for repair, maintenance and modernisation in your home.
tax.sections.hh.guidance.excludes: Material costs, new construction, cash payments.
tax.sections.hh.guidance.receipts: Invoices that show labour separately, proof of the bank transfer; tenants also find eligible costs in the service charge statement.
tax.sections.hh.guidance.note: Only labour, travel and machine costs including VAT count, and only when paid by bank transfer, so take them from the invoice, not from this total.
tax.sections.ki.name: Childcare and school fees
tax.sections.ki.guidance.belongs: Childcare (Kita, day nursery, childminder, after-school care), school fees for private schools.
tax.sections.ki.guidance.excludes: Meals, private tutoring, sports and music lessons.
tax.sections.ki.guidance.note: Childcare costs only count when paid to the provider's account, not in cash.
tax.sections.v.name: Renting and leasing
tax.sections.v.guidance.belongs: Rent and service charges received, and for the rented property: loan interest, maintenance, property tax, insurance and management fees.
tax.sections.v.guidance.excludes: Loan repayments (only the interest counts) and costs of your own home.
tax.sections.v.guidance.receipts: Rental contracts, loan statements, invoices, service charge statements.
tax.sections.v.guidance.note: The purchase price is depreciated over years and does not appear in your payments.
